---
title: "True Negative"
description: "A negative prediction that correctly matches a negative ground-truth label."
term: "True Negative"
letter: "T"
category: "Model Evaluation"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

A true negative is a case the model labels negative that really is
negative. For example, a spam filter correctly leaves a legitimate message
in the inbox.

## Technical explanation

In binary classification, a true negative (TN) occurs when the predicted
class is negative and the reference label is negative. TN is one cell of
the confusion matrix and contributes to metrics such as specificity and
accuracy.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

True negatives show how often a model correctly rejects non-target cases.
They are important when false alarms matter, but a large TN count can
dominate accuracy when the negative class is common.

## How it works

Define the negative class and classification threshold, compare model
predictions to ground-truth labels, and count cases where both are
negative. Interpret the count alongside the dataset size and other
confusion-matrix cells.

## Practical example

If a test set contains 900 legitimate messages and the classifier correctly
labels 855 as legitimate, those 855 are true negatives; the remaining
legitimate messages are false positives.

## Common misconceptions

- A true negative is not a measure of how many positive examples the model
  catches; that relates to recall.
- A high true-negative count alone may simply reflect a large negative
  class.
